newsitem.title: MEXICO: GCC estimates '96 cement sales up 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: GCC estimates '96 cement sales up 6 pct.

text.p: Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua (GCC) estimates its domestic cement sales volume in 1996 will be six percent more than in 1995, a company spokesman told Reuters.
"In 1996, we expect our Mexico cement sales to reach 590,000 or 600,000 tonnes, or six percent more than in 1995," said Jaime Fernandez, GCC spokesman.
Fernandez also estimated that cement output from the company's Tijeras, New Mexico plant would "increase by about nine percent compared with 1995, to reach up to 433,000 tonnes."
GCC meanwhile estimated that its exports to the U.S. in 1996 would increase to 400,000 tonnes in 1996, or more than 55 percent up from the 257,000 tonnes sold in 1995.
"We thus estimate a total sales volume of approximately 1.4 million tonnes, which is about 5.5 percent more than in 1995," he said.
Ready-mixed concrete sales were estimated at 302,000 cubic meters for 1996, or 10 percent more than in 1995.

GCC is a regional cement company whose main area of influence is in the northern Mexican state of Chihuahua, as well as parts of the U.S. states of Arizona, New Mexico and Texas. The company has an installed capacity of 2.375 million tonnes per year.
